opening_message: There's a vine that's taken over my fence and climbed up into a tree in the yard. Anyone know what kind of vine this actually is?

slots.name: seed_pod_texture
slots.value: There are a few old dried-up seed pods hanging on it from last year, and they're smooth, not fuzzy.
slots.description: Seed pod texture — smooth pods indicate American wisteria (Wisteria frutescens); velvety/fuzzy pods indicate the invasive Chinese wisteria. This is the single most decisive identification test available.

slots.name: bloom_timing
slots.value: It bloomed this past spring, but not until after the leaves had already come out on it.
slots.description: Bloom timing relative to leaf-out — American wisteria blooms after the leaves emerge; Chinese wisteria blooms before or as the leaves emerge. A second, independent confirmation of species alongside pod texture.

slots.name: growth_extent
slots.value: It's climbed maybe 15 feet up into an oak tree at the edge of the yard, and it covers a good stretch of the fence too.
slots.description: How far the vine has spread — doesn't change the correct identification or framing, since the correct answer (no treatment) doesn't depend on how much of it there is once identity is confirmed.

slots.name: years_present
slots.value: It's been there for as long as they can remember, at least ten years, just never really thought about it before.
slots.description: How long the vine has been established — background color, doesn't change the identification or framing.

slots.name: flower_color_fragrance
slots.value: The flowers were a light purple color and hung down in clusters, but they didn't smell like much of anything.
slots.description: Flower color/fragrance — both wisteria species have broadly similar purple, fragrant-to-mildly-fragrant flower clusters, so this isn't a reliable distinguishing feature on its own and shouldn't move the recommendation either way; included as a plausible but non-decisive detail a real user might offer.

slots.name: nearby_desirable_plants
slots.value: There's a vegetable garden on the other side of the yard, not too close to the fence or the tree.
slots.description: Proximity to desirable plants — would matter for drift/contact risk if herbicide were being used, but no herbicide is warranted here regardless, so it doesn't change the recommendation.

ecological_framing_notes: American wisteria is a native, non-invasive vine and larval host plant for several butterfly species, with real wildlife value. A correct answer should identify it as American wisteria (not the invasive Chinese wisteria), citing the smooth seed pods and/or after-leaf-out bloom timing, note that no cutting or herbicide is needed, and ideally encourage keeping it rather than merely declining to treat it.
